assessments.reasoning: The title page identifies the authors and the JKU publication record connects this author copy to the 1991 paper. Fresh HTTP 200 yielded the retained complete PDF, SHA-256 8812e21426954c0e17100bd0e3f2ce0a5c24b8ef6cc8dbddb0bff12fdf8848e7. Checked page streams and rendered page witnesses. Printed p. 5 (physical PDF p. 5), §6.2 Array types, last paragraph before examples; printed p. 6 (physical PDF p. 6), §6.4 Pointer types, first NEW paragraph; printed p. 17 (physical PDF p. 17), §10.3 Proper procedures table, NEW rows. Section 6.2 lists pointer base types as a permitted open-array context. Section 6.4 explains allocation and pointer assignment. The NEW table distinguishes this operation from record and fixed-array allocation. The length expressions provide the dimensions at allocation. The first argument is a pointer variable in both the pointer section and the predeclared procedure table. The first argument is a variable whose pointer base type is an open array. An n-dimensional open array uses n length arguments. This applies to the 26-page JKU language report. The earlier May 1991 ETH TR160 note presents a differently spelled direct open-array variable example and is outside the claim's edition. TR160 printed p. 5 uses direct open-array declaration syntax in its example. That earlier example does not broaden the pointer form or declare its availability in the JKU report.
